Mission

Reusable rockets. Built in India. Open to the world.

India's first next-generation, high-power rocket propulsion lab, developing fully reusable launch vehicles powered by Methalox engines. Our goal is affordable space access for every nation, company and person.

Build

India's first high-power Methalox propulsion lab and engine test facility.

Develop

A fully reusable launch vehicle system with booster and upper stage recovery.

Enable

Affordable access to space for startups, researchers and developing nations.

The problem

Orbit is priced like a luxury good.

Five structural problems keep space closed to most of the world, and India still has no reusable rocket of its own.

COST

$2,000 to $6,000 per kg

Most launch vehicles are only partially reusable, which keeps the price of every flight high.

ACCESS

Closed to emerging nations

Long waits and few launch slots lock out startups, researchers and developing economies.

INDIA

No reusable Indian rocket

There is no fully reusable Indian launch vehicle and no domestic liquid engine in service. India still depends on solid motors.

PROPELLANT

Dirty fuels dominate

Kerosene and solid propellants pollute the atmosphere, and no green propulsion standard exists yet.

EQUITY

Out of reach for most

Universities, small companies and individuals have no affordable way to send a payload to orbit.

What makes us different

Full reuse, built around a cleaner flame.

Methalox engine

A 50 kN engine, then 200 kN.

50kN

Methane and liquid oxygen burn clean, run well with cryogenic handling and suit many reuses. Our first target is a 50 kN Methalox engine, with a 200 kN class engine after that.

Combustion chambers are 3D printed, which cuts weight and cost and lets us iterate in days instead of months.

Reusable hardware

Built to fly again.

Our reusable titanium nozzle is designed to extend engine life and cut refurbishment time and cost. Patent work is in progress.

Boosters and upper stages are meant to return and land, so both stages can be refurbished and flown again. AI-assisted engine health monitoring supports fast inspection and go or no-go decisions between flights.

Propulsion lab first

Test infrastructure comes first.

We are setting up India's first high-power Methalox propulsion lab, with the test stands needed to develop engines properly. We have already designed and built our own solid motor and a 10 kN thrust stand.

A large 3D-printed two-piece rocket body keeps the structure fast to build, low in cost and easy to refurbish.

Recovery

Both stages come back.

STAGE 1

Ascent

Methalox engines carry the vehicle to separation.

STAGE 2

Separation

The upper stage continues to orbit while the booster turns back.

STAGE 3

Return

The booster returns under control toward the landing site.

STAGE 4

Powered landing

A vertical or sea landing recovers the stage intact.

STAGE 5

Refly

Health data guides a fast inspection, then the stage flies again.

Traction

We have already flown rockets.

Before founding Singularity Space, our core team put its propulsion and recovery work in the air, not just on paper.

Prometheus

First supersonic experimental rocket we developed in India, reaching 3.3 km altitude at about Mach 1.4.

L-class solid motor

Designed, manufactured and static-fire tested in-house, with a 10 kN thrust stand and launch infrastructure.

Liquid engine

A bi-propellant liquid engine, with work on its combustion system, feed system, valves and test infrastructure. It is the base for our Methalox program.

Roadmap

Flight profile: 0 to 60 months.

0 – 12 months

Lab and patent foundation

  • Complete 50 kN Methalox engine manufacturing
  • Establish propulsion lab and test infrastructure
  • Finalize reusable nozzle patent
6 – 18 months

First hot-fire and recovery demo

  • Hot-fire the 50 kN Methalox engine
  • Build and test a subscale reusable booster

18 – 36 months

Scale to 200 kN

  • Develop a 200 kN class engine
  • Begin suborbital and orbital prototype testing
  • Secure first commercial contracts
36 – 60 months

First commercial orbital mission

  • Fly the first full commercial reusable orbital mission
  • Start medium-lift vehicle development
  • Test in-space refueling concepts
